issues: Teaching labels (Sister_A, Sister_B, Pole, Microtubule) are already baked into the pixels, though the spec states labels are added after generation; non-blocking but a pipeline deviation.

observations: Frame 1 shows a single duplicated chromosome: two parallel pink chromatid bars (Sister_A, Sister_B) joined at the centromeric region, centered on the vertical metaphase-plate line, i.e. aligned at the equator.

Frame 1 shows bipolar kinetochore-microtubule attachment: left-pole microtubule binds the left kinetochore (yellow dot on Sister_A), right-pole microtubule binds the right kinetochore (yellow dot on Sister_B); sister kinetochores face opposite poles as required.

Frame 2 shows the same two sisters separated to opposite halves: Sister_A on the left with its left-pole microtubule-kinetochore attachment retained, Sister_B on the right with its right-pole attachment retained.

Identity tracking is consistent across endpoints: Sister_A -> left pole in both frames, Sister_B -> right pole in both frames, so poleward direction is verifiable from the two labeled endpoints (no direction ambiguity).
Chromatid count is conserved: exactly two chromatids in frame 1 and exactly two in frame 2; no extra copies and no loss, satisfying 'persistent sisters, no copies'.
No cohesin cleavage is depicted, consistent with the declared out-of-scope molecular mechanism; only the observable connection breakdown and separation are shown.
limitations: Only first/last frames were provided; intermediate trajectory is not verified, so continuous poleward motion and the exact moment of connection breakdown are assumed rather than observed.

In frame 1 the two kinetochore dots are very close together at the center, making the left-vs-right microtubule binding slightly ambiguous at pixel level, though the bipolar reading is the natural and intended one.
In frame 2 the chromatids are on the correct opposite sides but not yet at the poles; acceptable as a schematic anaphase endpoint but not a fully pole-arrived state.
Topology is a simplified two-bar schematic (parallel chromatids joined at a point), appropriate for grades 10-12 but not a realistic condensed-chromosome morphology.
Scope is a single modeled chromosome pair; this validates the schematic instantiation only, not the universal 'all chromosomes' alignment statement.
